name: Numbers In Narrative Rubric
description: Evaluation criteria for prose that carries quantities: whether the numbers land for a reader and whether they stay inside what the sources support

criteria.name: Frame Lock and Denominator Discipline
criteria.description: Whether unit, denominator, window and population boundary are fixed in writing, and whether the denominator holds across the whole piece

scores.1: No frame stated; denominators switch between counts, rates and shares across the piece with no acknowledgement
scores.2: Frame implied but never written; at least one unnarrated denominator switch survives into the final text
scores.3: Frame written for unit and denominator; window and boundary unjustified; denominator sweep not run
scores.4: All four locked with justification; denominator sweep run; any switch is narrated as a beat
scores.5: All four locked with one rejected alternative and a reason each; sweep table produced; rate-vs-count rule applied and any moving denominator shown as both series

criteria.name: Number Landing
criteria.description: Whether each surviving figure is legible: budget respected, rounded appropriately, compared, at human scale, direction before magnitude

scores.1: Stat walls throughout; bare figures with no comparison; paragraphs open cold on numbers the reader has no frame for
scores.2: Some comparisons present but budgets ignored; magnitude given before direction; precision carried unnecessarily
scores.3: Budgets mostly respected and most figures compared; human-scale conversion inconsistent
scores.4: Budgets respected; every figure compared on the same screen; direction precedes magnitude; frames built before figures land
scores.5: As 4, plus human-scale conversions that do not overclaim, rounding tested against the specific claim each sentence makes, and bureaucratic number-words replaced without breaking terms of art

criteria.name: Source Fidelity and Precision
criteria.description: Whether figures stay inside their sources: precision ceiling, rounding drift, percent vs percentage point, relative vs absolute, contested values, ranges

scores.1: Figures exceed source precision; derived numbers computed from rounded prose; percent and percentage point conflated; contested figures silently resolved
scores.2: Precision mostly respected but at least one derived figure traces to a prose number, or one contested figure was picked without disclosure
scores.3: Precision ceiling held and contested figures carry both values; totals not recomputed from held values at the end
scores.4: No precision violations; all derived figures computed from held source values; percent/point and relative/absolute correct throughout; ranges survive into prose
scores.5: As 4, plus end-of-draft recomputation of every total and share from held values, parts confirmed to sum, and every figure resolving to an external pointer with no circular sourcing

criteria.name: Epistemic Grammar
criteria.description: Whether the sentence shape matches the evidentiary status: measurement vs model, trend claims, qualitative quantifiers, sourced vs verified, intentionality verbs on systems

scores.1: Model output written as observation; trends asserted from two points; qualitative quantifiers converted to numerals; work described as verified
scores.2: Occasional model-as-measurement slips or an unmarked two-point trend; system intentionality verbs used freely
scores.3: Model output marked and two-point trends avoided; some intentionality verbs on systems remain unmarked
scores.4: Every projection, fit or estimate carries model grammar; no manufactured numerals; provenance language says sourced, not verified
scores.5: As 4, plus system intentionality either rewritten as aggregated behaviour of named actors or marked once as an explicit device, and no verb carrying a hidden causal claim survives

criteria.name: Uncertainty Routing
criteria.description: Whether uncertainty is typed and routed to a vehicle and a placement, rather than dumped in a methods note or smeared across every sentence

scores.1: Uncertainty absent, or entirely confined to a trailing methods note
scores.2: Uncertainty present but untyped and placed by habit; or hedges appear in nearly every sentence so nothing lands
scores.3: Dominant type named for most load-bearing claims and routed roughly by table; momentum rule not applied
scores.4: One type per claim, routed to the correct vehicle and placement; momentum rule applied so only conclusion-changing uncertainty takes its own beat
scores.5: As 4, plus reference-model sentences written for load-bearing claims, missingness rendered rather than left blank, and specification disagreement made the beat where two defensible specifications diverge

criteria.name: Likelihood and Confidence Discipline
criteria.description: Whether banded language is declared, consistent, separated from confidence, and reserved for load-bearing judgments

scores.1: Probability words used loosely and interchangeably; likelihood and confidence combined in single sentences
scores.2: Some banded terms used but no ladder declared, and terms drift between sections
scores.3: A ladder is declared but applied to too many non-load-bearing sentences, or the two ladders occasionally blend
scores.4: Ladder declared once in the piece; terms hold their bands; likelihood and confidence always separated
scores.5: As 4, plus banding restricted to judgments a reader would act on, no banded term paired with a contradicting bare number, and the ladder's status as a declared convention rather than a universal standard made explicit

criteria.name: Exhibit Contract
criteria.description: Whether each exhibit carrying a beat has a checkable title, falsification lines, a leap-of-faith mark and survives detachment

scores.1: Exhibits titled as labels; no annotation discipline; projected values indistinguishable from measured ones
scores.2: Titles carry claims but no falsification line was written; caveats live only in the surrounding prose
scores.3: Beat sentence written before drawing and title made a claim; density caps or the detachment test skipped
scores.4: Beat, checkable title, density caps, leap-of-faith mark, and a falsification line per annotation
scores.5: As 4, plus the exhibit passing the detachment test carrying both beat and caveat, provenance on the exhibit, and consistent encodings across the sequence

criteria.name: Omission and Over-Disclosure Balance
criteria.description: Whether cuts were reviewed as a set and whether counter-evidence is findable, without answering the audit by burying the reader in caveats

scores.1: No record of what was cut; disconfirming figures absent; or the draft is padded with caveat exhibits that obscure the argument
scores.2: Cuts made ad hoc with no log; strongest counter-evidence appears late or not at all
scores.3: Omitted-number log kept but reviewed per cut rather than as a set
scores.4: Log reviewed as a set for shared direction; counter-evidence present and reachable; hedge budget respected
scores.5: As 4, plus a disagreeing reader able to find the strongest counter-number within one exhibit of where they are, and no defensive volume added in place of a reversal

passing_note: Average score must be >= 3.5. Scores below 3 in 'Frame Lock and Denominator Discipline' or 'Source Fidelity and Precision' require revision regardless of the average, because both failures survive fact-checking.
